common_freshwater_1.name: Shinefish
common_freshwater_1.description: Small shiny freshwater fish, often fished in massive quantities. Its meat is often used in cheap transformed dishes and its scales is used for dyes.

common_freshwater_2.name: Sanamon
common_freshwater_2.description: Common medium freshwater fish often fished for its pink meat associated with gourmet meals. Is intentionnaly heavily fished as it spreads faster than any other species. This makes it commonly used in dishes in low income families as well as classy restaurants.

common_freshwater_3.name: Gilly
common_freshwater_3.description: Small freshwater fish with fancy gills. Has really smooth scales that tickles. Despite this, its scales can be used for toys manufacturing and its meat is often used to accompany rice.

common_freshwater_4.name: Barss
common_freshwater_4.description: Heavy freshwater fish commonly found around popular fishing spots. This species is very competitive in nature, and will fight with its own kin, which led to them being easily lured by bait.

common_freshwater_5.name: Prach
common_freshwater_5.description: Medium freshwater fish. Playful and curious, it plays with its food before eating. Its curiousity have led to them to be fished in great quantities, which led to regulations about their capture (this season is a good one, don't worry).

uncommon_freshwater_1.name: Golden Shinefish
uncommon_freshwater_1.description: Cousin to the shinefish, these fishes are distinct due to their big eyes and golden scales. Their scale can be used not for dyes, but for shiny gloden glitter, and their meat has been acknoledged by the greatest chef, as a great palette cleanser due to its spongy and tasteless nature.

uncommon_freshwater_2.name: Big Eyed Garen
uncommon_freshwater_2.description: A medium fish known for its long mouth and big eye. Seen in ancient times as the watchful eye of the gods, these fishes were kept around in houses to keep watch on naughty children. They are still used like that, but are also made into food, as you'd expect. Their meat is often used in spicy recipies.

uncommon_freshwater_3.name: Chuppo
uncommon_freshwater_3.description: A medium sized fish that loves fighting other species when young, making them likely to die before maturing. When matured, this bahaviour stops, and their scales start falling off before growing back These falling scales have been used in medications that help anger management ; and their meat is naturally fat, reducing the heart rate of anyone who eats it.

rare_freshwater_1.name: Kittyfish
rare_freshwater_1.description: Very large freshwater fish. It has whiskers which has led to its name. They are howver not fans of petting nor scratches. They do however have strength as great as their appetite.

rare_freshwater_2.name: Sage babel
rare_freshwater_2.description: Rare medium fish with weird mustache prongs at its mouth. Despite being named after the tower of Babel, this fish does not speak multiple languages. However, it does have superior cognition, which has led to it being hard to fish.

unusual_freshwater_1.name: Chromafish
unusual_freshwater_1.description: An unusual and very small freshwater fish that only resides in rivers. Very playful and fast, he loves to ride the current up, and can go from the sea to the water source within a couple days. He shines of every color the human eye can see, even magenta.

unusual_freshwater_2.name: Muckychup
unusual_freshwater_2.description: An unusual variant of the Chuppo, this fish loves to cover itself in algae, gunk and other weird gooey substances to hide among predators and fishermen. Very few chups get the urge to do so, and with no reason to point to, making scientist scratch their heads at this chup variant's mere existence.

legendary_freshwater_1.name: The Great Descendant
legendary_freshwater_1.description: The Great Descendant is a very very rare freshwater fish, even scientists can't pin-point its origin. It is speculated to be the king of fishes, a descendant of the dinosaurs that found refuge in water and that barely evolved. From what scientists gathered, he `is a really big boy, and probably is just almost extinct.` You just might have the very last of his kind. Be nice to him.
